subject: Follow-up: service tiering, token targets & model allocation (Acme Retail)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: service tiering, token targets & model allocation (Acme Retail)

Hi Alicia — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so your team can share with procurement: 

1) Volume & budget signals
- You indicated a target of 50M tokens/month ramping to 200M over 3 quarters.
- Procurement asked for a 3-tier cost envelope: conservative (50M), expected (120M), stretch (200M).
- Target blended cost target: $1,100 / 1M tokens for the initial pilot, trending toward $800 / 1M at scale depending on model mix and caching.

2) Model mix (recommended starting split)
- Chat (conversational generation): 60% of tokens (primary user journeys).
- Embeddings (search & semantic features): 30% of tokens — heavy embedding creation on ingest, smaller per-query cost.
- Rerank (embedding-based rerank calls): 10% of tokens.

3) Service tiers & SLAs
- Pilot: shared hosted tier with committed burst capacity, 99.9% uptime, token-level billing.
- Production/dedicated: Dedicated pool option with reserved throughput and stricter latency SLOs.

4) Action items
- Acme: confirm expected month-1 volume (conservative/expected/stretch) and any compliance docs needed from SOC2 summary (you mentioned legal wants a short writeup).
- Redwood (Ben/Vanessa): attach pricing worksheet with per-model unit economics and a draft mutual action plan for signatures.

I attached the pricing worksheet and SOC2 summary for quick review. If these numbers look directionally correct, Ben will sketch a 3-month pilot quote with per-model unit rates and caching assumptions.

Proposed next call: 48 hours — procurement + engineering + our solutions engineer to lock on final pilot volume and sign MPA. Is Thursday 10am PT okay?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (pricing workbook), SOC2-summary.pdf (controls summary), mutual-action-plan-acme.docx (draft MPA)
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2028-05-04T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: service tiering, token targets & model allocation (Acme Retail)

Thanks Naomi — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 50M to 200M timeline is accurate but likely 90 days to hit 120M, 180 days to hit 200M (depends on campaign schedule).
- The $1,100 / 1M target for pilot is okay as a starting point; procurement will push for a stretch discount at 200M.
- Can you include assumed cache hit-rate in the pricing worksheet? Our engineering lead wants to see sensitivity to 10%/30%/50% cache hit (prefix + KV).

Also, legal asked: are there data locality guarantees for the hosted tier? If not, share the Dedicated/Private pricing and a summary of network egress assumptions.

Thursday 10am PT works for the 48-hour slot. Please add your solutions engineer and the person who owns Dedicated pricing.

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, Acme Retail
alicia.gomez@acme.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: service tiering, token targets & model allocation (Acme Retail)

Alicia — adding more detail on unit economics and cache sensitivity. Numbers are approximate but reflect realistic kernel/quantization options for the models we discussed. See the short summary below; full workbook attached.

Assumptions (pilot):
- Baseline chat model (gen-3b equivalent) cost: $1,250 / 1M tokens without caching. With 30% effective prefix/KV cache, effective blended cost moves to ~$950 / 1M.
- Embeddings (dense encoder) cost: $200 / 1M tokens (note: embeddings creation is heavy up-front but per-query costs are lower due to reuse and vector DB caching).
- Rerank (small cross-encoder): $1,600 / 1M tokens but used sparingly — we show an amortized add of ~$120 / 1M to the blended cost at a 10% volume share.

Example blended math (expected 120M/month, 30% cache hit):
- Chat 60% => 72M tokens x $950/1M => $68,400
- Embeddings 30% => 36M tokens x $200/1M => $7,200
- Rerank 10% => 12M tokens x $1,600/1M => $19,200
- Total month cost => $94,800 => blended $790 / 1M tokens

Notes:
- If cache hit improves to 50%, chat effective falls to ~$800/1M and blended goes to ~$710/1M at 120M.
- Dedicated pricing (reserved capacity) will further reduce per-token by 10-35% depending on commit and burst profile — will prepare a table for Thursday.

Next steps from my side: attach a worksheet with 3 cache scenarios and dedicated vs hosted comparison. I also included a short 'what's included' for the Dedicated pool (latency SLOs, isolation).

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Ben — these numbers are helpful, thanks. A couple quick asks before the Thursday call: 

1) Can you show the blended $/1M at 50% chat cache and at the 200M scale? Procurement wants a clear best-case/worst-case.
2) For rerank: what are typical invocation patterns you see (e.g., rerank per query vs per session)? We want to size the vector DB and estimate downstream infra.

Also, procurement wants the draft mutual action plan shared as a single Google Doc (not Word) so they can edit. Can you convert and share a Drive link?

Thanks,
Alicia
